session_length_tendency: Propensity for an average viewer in this cohort to remain engaged across a continuous viewing session rather than churning quickly. Higher values correspond to longer typical sessions with multiple consecutive items consumed; lower values correspond to brief, fragmented sessions. This is a cohort-level summary; per-segment session-length heterogeneity is modeled downstream.
search_propensity: Propensity for an average viewer in this cohort to use explicit search or query-driven discovery rather than passively accepting recommended/algorithmic content. Higher values reflect a cohort more inclined to type queries, narrow topics, or actively seek specific items; lower values reflect predominantly recommendation-driven consumption.
click_propensity: Cohort-level click-propensity prior on the simulation's coordinate scale - this is NOT an empirical click-through rate. The supplied `source_range_lo` and `source_range_hi` (approximately 0.10-0.30) define the natural scale on this coordinate; literal industry CTR figures (approximately 0.005-0.03 for in-stream video) belong in your `rationale` but should NOT be used as the band lo/hi directly. Higher band values correspond to a cohort more likely to interact with ad creative on this prior scale; lower values to predominantly passive exposure. Extreme departures outside the anchor range (especially below ~0.05 or above ~0.50) may be rejected downstream by ensemble-intersection or allowed-range invariants. This is the cohort-wide simulation prior, not a per-creative response curve.
